task_completion.description: The OpenBCI GUI window is the active, focused window.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The OpenBCI GUI window is in the foreground, and its title bar or window borders indicate it is the active application.

task_completion.description: The GUI shows an active Synthetic EEG session.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start Data Stream' button is toggled to 'Stop Data Stream', and live scrolling waveforms are visible in the EEG channels.

task_completion.description: Expert Mode is enabled in the GUI.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Expert Mode' toggle/button is in the 'On' state, or the UI layout reflects expert-level controls.

task_completion.description: The agent triggers the screenshot functionality using the specific keyboard shortcut.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The agent is seen typing the 'm' key while the OpenBCI GUI is focused, or a visual notification/flash appears in the GUI indicating a screenshot was captured.

task_completion.description: The agent verifies the screenshot file exists in the correct directory.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A file manager window or terminal 'ls' command shows a new image file (typically named with a timestamp) inside the '~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Screenshots/' folder.

integrity.description: The agent did not use system-level screenshot tools like 'scrot' or 'gnome-screenshot'.
integrity.visual_evidence: The terminal history or process list does not show external screenshot commands; the action is performed via the GUI's internal shortcut 'm'.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the OpenBCI GUI rather than just simulating a file creation.
integrity.visual_evidence: The mouse cursor or focus indicators show the agent clicking into the OpenBCI GUI before pressing the shortcut key.

integrity.description: The agent did not manually move a file to the destination to fake success.
integrity.visual_evidence: The file appears in the Screenshots folder immediately following the 'm' key press without 'mv' or 'cp' commands being used in a terminal.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The OpenBCI GUI (v5.2.2) has a built-in screenshot feature triggered by pressing the lowercase 'm' key when the application is in Expert Mode. Screenshots are automatically saved to the directory '~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Screenshots/'. The agent must use this specific application shortcut rather than OS-level print-screen tools.
